=== obsbot4linux --help
Control the OBSBOT Tiny 2 Lite

Usage: obsbot4linux [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  daemon                   Run the daemon: owns the camera, serves the socket, broadcasts state changes
  watch                    Stream state events as JSON lines and forward JSON requests from stdin (for widgets)
  live-pose                Ask the daemon to poll the gimbal pose for this connection (a `watch` request; the daemon polls it every second only while a connection wants it). Not usable as a one-off call
  detect                   Exit 0 and print the model (--json: model and video device) when a supported camera is connected, exit 1 with no output when not. Enumeration only: no daemon, no camera command
  status                   Show all settings (the camera's status block, tracking readback, zoom, image controls, remembered state)
  sleep                    Put the camera to sleep
  wake                     Wake the camera, or set the stored wake-up zoom (`wake zoom`) or the tracking mode at power-on (`wake mode`)
  tracking                 AI tracking mode
  speed                    Tracking type: standard, sport (fixed fast gain) or headroom (more room above the head)
  speed-mode               Fine tracking speed, from lazy to very-fast, or auto. Ignored while `speed sport` is set or the part mode is not normal
  framing                  Framing options of the human tracking; an AI mode change overwrites them
  hdr                      HDR
  exposure                 Exposure: automatic metering over the whole picture (global) or on faces (face), or manual, optionally with the shutter time and gain (`image gain` sets the gain too; `image exposure_time` is refused unless the exposure is already manual)
  zoom                     Zoom factor 1.0-4.0; with --speed the camera zooms smoothly instead of jumping
  gimbal                   Move the gimbal to an absolute pose in degrees (switches tracking to static first), or `gimbal stop|rate`
  fov                      Field of view (ignored by the camera while it sleeps)
  led                      Status LED: brightness 0 (off) to 3, or `led blink on|off`
  mirror                   Mirror the image
  invert                   Invert view and gimbal (reverses the gimbal's pan direction)
  auto-sleep               Auto-sleep: "off" or a time in seconds
  sleep-background         Picture shown while the camera sleeps
  sleep-background-mirror  Mirror the sleep background
  audio                    Microphone settings
  gesture                  Gesture control
  hand                     Hand tracking: which hand, return position, area, axes
  zone                     Zone tracking
  focus                    Focus: autofocus mode, continuous autofocus, manual focus
  startup                  Initial state: the pose the camera moves to when it powers on
  image                    UVC image control, e.g. "image brightness 128" (names are in "status")
  preset                   Presets stored in the camera (slots 0-2)
  factory-reset            Reset the camera to factory settings (it restarts and deletes its presets)
  help                     Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --json     Print machine-readable JSON (errors too, as {"ok":false,"error":...})
      --direct   Do not use a running daemon; talk to the camera directly
  -h, --help     Print help
  -V, --version  Print version
=== obsbot4linux daemon --help

Options:

      --direct  Do not use a running daemon; talk to the camera directly
  -h, --help    Print help

=== obsbot4linux wake --help
Wake the camera, or set the stored wake-up zoom (`wake zoom`) or the tracking mode at power-on (`wake mode`)

Usage: obsbot4linux wake [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]

Commands:
  zoom  Stored wake-up zoom, factor 1.0-4.0 (the camera stores 0-100 percent). Effect unknown on the Tiny 2 Lite: no change at power-on or on waking from sleep
  mode  Tracking mode the camera starts in at power-on, not on waking from sleep (the current mode stays)
  help  Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --json    Print machine-readable JSON (errors too, as {"ok":false,"error":...})
      --direct  Do not use a running daemon; talk to the camera directly
  -h, --help    Print help
=== obsbot4linux wake zoom --help

Arguments:
  <FACTOR>  

Options:
      --json    Print machine-readable JSON (errors too, as {"ok":false,"error":...})

  -h, --help    Print help

=== obsbot4linux framing --help
Framing options of the human tracking; an AI mode change overwrites them

Usage: obsbot4linux framing [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  auto-zoom   Auto zoom of the human tracking on or off
  size        Size of the auto zoom framing
  zoom-speed  How fast the auto zoom follows
  offset      Shift the framing by a fraction of the frame, -0.16 to 0.16
  part        Which part of the body the framing follows
  help        Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --json    Print machine-readable JSON (errors too, as {"ok":false,"error":...})
      --direct  Do not use a running daemon; talk to the camera directly
  -h, --help    Print help

=== obsbot4linux exposure --help
Exposure: automatic metering over the whole picture (global) or on faces (face), or manual, optionally with the shutter time and gain (`image gain` sets the gain too; `image exposure_time` is refused unless the exposure is already manual)

Usage: obsbot4linux exposure [OPTIONS] <MODE>

Arguments:
  <MODE>  [possible values: global, face, manual]

Options:
      --json         Print machine-readable JSON (errors too, as {"ok":false,"error":...})
      --time <TIME>  Manual only: shutter time in 100 us units, 1-2500 (330 is one frame at 30 fps); the camera uses the step at or below it
      --direct       Do not use a running daemon; talk to the camera directly
      --gain <GAIN>  Manual only: gain 1-64 (ISO is gain x 100)
  -h, --help         Print help
=== obsbot4linux zoom --help
Zoom factor 1.0-4.0; with --speed the camera zooms smoothly instead of jumping

Usage: obsbot4linux zoom [OPTIONS] [FACTOR]
       obsbot4linux zoom <COMMAND>

Commands:
  stop  Stop a zoom in progress
  help  Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Arguments:
  [FACTOR]  

Options:
      --json           Print machine-readable JSON (errors too, as {"ok":false,"error":...})
      --speed <SPEED>  Zoom speed (OBSBOT Center uses 30; the auto zoom 10, 30, 50)
      --direct         Do not use a running daemon; talk to the camera directly
  -h, --help           Print help
=== obsbot4linux zoom stop --help

Usage: obsbot4linux zoom stop [OPTIONS]

      --json    Print machine-readable JSON (errors too, as {"ok":false,"error":...})
      --direct  Do not use a running daemon; talk to the camera directly
  -h, --help    Print help
=== obsbot4linux gimbal --help
Move the gimbal to an absolute pose in degrees (switches tracking to static first), or `gimbal stop|rate`

Usage: obsbot4linux gimbal [OPTIONS]
       obsbot4linux gimbal <COMMAND>

Commands:
  stop  Stop all gimbal axes (also a `gimbal rate` still running)
  rate  Keep turning at a speed in degrees per second (up to 178) UNTIL `gimbal stop` or a speed of 0, also when the client is gone; like the joystick of OBSBOT Center (switches tracking to static first). An axis you leave out is stopped: `--pan 5` alone also stops a running tilt turn
  help  Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --json           Print machine-readable JSON (errors too, as {"ok":false,"error":...})
      --pan <PAN>      Positive turns the camera to its left
      --direct         Do not use a running daemon; talk to the camera directly
      --tilt <TILT>    Positive tilts the camera up
      --speed <SPEED>  Take as long as this many degrees per second (1-180) need instead of going as fast as possible
  -h, --help           Print help
=== obsbot4linux gimbal stop --help
Stop all gimbal axes (also a `gimbal rate` still running)

Usage: obsbot4linux gimbal stop [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --json    Print machine-readable JSON (errors too, as {"ok":false,"error":...})
      --direct  Do not use a running daemon; talk to the camera directly
  -h, --help    Print help
=== obsbot4linux gimbal rate --help
Keep turning at a speed in degrees per second (up to 178) UNTIL `gimbal stop` or a speed of 0, also when the client is gone; like the joystick of OBSBOT Center (switches tracking to static first). An axis you leave out is stopped: `--pan 5` alone also stops a running tilt turn

Usage: obsbot4linux gimbal rate [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --json         Print machine-readable JSON (errors too, as {"ok":false,"error":...})
      --pan <PAN>    Positive turns the camera to its left
      --direct       Do not use a running daemon; talk to the camera directly
      --tilt <TILT>  Positive tilts the camera up
  -h, --help         Print help

=== obsbot4linux audio --help
Microphone settings

Usage: obsbot4linux audio [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  noise      Microphone noise reduction
  gain       Automatic gain
  distance   Pickup distance
  volume     Microphone volume 0-100 (below 50 reads as near, 50-84 standard, from 85 far)
  sleep-mic  Keep the microphone on while the camera sleeps
  mic        Microphone on/off; every change makes the camera restart (about 18 s)
  help       Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --json    Print machine-readable JSON (errors too, as {"ok":false,"error":...})
      --direct  Do not use a running daemon; talk to the camera directly
  -h, --help    Print help

=== obsbot4linux hand --help
Hand tracking: which hand, return position, area, axes

Usage: obsbot4linux hand [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  right         Track the right hand
  left          Track the left hand
  return-here   Take the current camera pose as the position the camera returns to after the hand leaves
  return-go     Move the camera to the hand-tracking return position
  return-reset  Clear the hand-tracking return position
  area          Area the hand is tracked in, in degrees. The camera's default: --pan -45 45 --tilt -30 30
  area-reset    Set the hand tracking area back to the camera's default
  pan           Whether the hand tracker may pan (off: the pan axis stays where it is)
  tilt          Whether the hand tracker may tilt (off: the tilt axis stays where it is)
  return-after  Seconds the hand may stay outside the area before the camera returns to the return position
  gimbal        Whether the hand tracker may move the gimbal at all (off stops it; the camera does not keep this setting)
  help          Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --json    Print machine-readable JSON (errors too, as {"ok":false,"error":...})
      --direct  Do not use a running daemon; talk to the camera directly
  -h, --help    Print help

  -h, --help    Print help

=== obsbot4linux hand area --help
Area the hand is tracked in, in degrees. The camera's default: --pan -45 45 --tilt -30 30

Usage: obsbot4linux hand area [OPTIONS] --pan <MIN> <MAX> --tilt <MIN> <MAX>

Options:
      --json              Print machine-readable JSON (errors too, as {"ok":false,"error":...})
      --pan <MIN> <MAX>   Pan range, MIN MAX, positive = camera left (-150..150)
      --direct            Do not use a running daemon; talk to the camera directly
      --tilt <MIN> <MAX>  Tilt range, MIN MAX, positive = up (-70..90)
  -h, --help              Print help

=== obsbot4linux hand tilt --help
Whether the hand tracker may tilt (off: the tilt axis stays where it is)

=== obsbot4linux zone --help
Zone tracking

Usage: obsbot4linux zone [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  on           
  off          
  follow       Automatically follow new targets
  area         Area the zone tracking stays in, in degrees. Full area: --pan -150 150 --tilt -70 90
  return-here  Take the current camera pose as the position the zone tracking returns to
  return-go    Move the camera to the zone return position
  view         Named poses stored in the camera ("zone views"); the camera does not track by them
  help         Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

=== obsbot4linux startup --help
Initial state: the pose the camera moves to when it powers on

Usage: obsbot4linux startup [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  set   Set the start pose: --pan/--tilt/--zoom, or --preset <slot>, or --current. There is no way known to clear it; pan 0, tilt 0, zoom 1 is the neutral start
  show  Show the start pose and the picture settings of the initial state
  go    Move the camera to the start pose now (the pose it takes at power-on)
  help  Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --json    Print machine-readable JSON (errors too, as {"ok":false,"error":...})
      --direct  Do not use a running daemon; talk to the camera directly
  -h, --help    Print help
=== obsbot4linux startup set --help
Set the start pose: --pan/--tilt/--zoom, or --preset <slot>, or --current. There is no way known to clear it; pan 0, tilt 0, zoom 1 is the neutral start

Usage: obsbot4linux startup set [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --json
          Print machine-readable JSON (errors too, as {"ok":false,"error":...})

      --pan <PAN>
          Positive turns the camera to its left

      --direct
          Do not use a running daemon; talk to the camera directly

      --tilt <TILT>
          Positive tilts the camera up

      --zoom <ZOOM>
          

      --preset <PRESET>
          Use the pose of a stored preset (slot as in "preset list", 0-2)

      --current
          Use the current pose (remembered gimbal pose, live zoom)

      --ai <AI>
          AI mode of the initial state (the camera tracks in it again after "startup go" and powers on in it). Kept as it is when not given; "none" clears it, and then "startup go" leaves tracking suspended. Alone, it leaves the pose untouched

          Possible values:
          - static
          - normal
          - upper-body
          - headless
          - group
          - none:       Not set (the camera's own default): `startup go` leaves tracking suspended

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
=== obsbot4linux startup show --help
Show the start pose and the picture settings of the initial state

Options:
      --json    Print machine-readable JSON (errors too, as {"ok":false,"error":...})
      --direct  Do not use a running daemon; talk to the camera directly
  -h, --help    Print help

=== obsbot4linux preset --help
Presets stored in the camera (slots 0-2)

Usage: obsbot4linux preset [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  list    List the presets
  save    Save a pose to a slot; without --pan/--tilt/--zoom the current pose is used (the last gimbal pose obsbot4linux sent, else the one V4L2 last set; live zoom)
  rename  Rename a preset (printable ASCII, up to 32 characters)
  delete  Delete a preset
  recall  Move the camera to a preset
  help    Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --json    Print machine-readable JSON (errors too, as {"ok":false,"error":...})
